title: Scraper bug: Supermicro hits 403 Forbidden on catalog (Akamai)
description:

1. 

Expected: 
Actual: 

The Supermicro scraper landed in CL-82 fails with HTTP 403 from Akamai when fetching
https://www.supermicro.com/support/resources/bios_ipmi.php?vendor=2 — the public AMD
catalog URL the scraper is built around.

## Reproduction

    $ uv run psp-etl scrape supermicro
    httpx.HTTPStatusError: Client error '403 Forbidden' for url
    'https://www.supermicro.com/support/resources/bios_ipmi.php?vendor=2'

## Root cause

The scraper sends a plain User-Agent. Supermicro is fronted by Akamai, which now
rejects datacenter / non-browser User-Agents on this endpoint. During the original
issue triage (CL-79 survey) the catalog returned 200 with a plain UA from a
residential IP — Akamai's filter has tightened since.

## Fix

Adopt the same browser-like header set the existing Gigabyte consumer scraper
uses (src/psp_etl/scrape/gigabyte.py:42-66 _HEADERS dict): full Chrome User-Agent
plus Sec-Fetch-* + sec-ch-ua + Accept-Language. Worked for Gigabyte's Akamai
front; should work for Supermicro's.

If Akamai escalates further, fall back to Wayback CDX over
www.supermicro.com/support/resources/downloadcenter/firmware/* (per-board pages
have the actual download URLs).

## Acceptance criteria

- `uv run psp-etl scrape supermicro --dry-run` lists at least 25 H11/H12/H13 boards
  without error
- existing tests still pass

Refs: CL-82 (original scraper), CL-79 (prior-art survey).
